findings.message: The nested-extends check treats any parent with frontmatter as nesting. That includes a local parent that only extends its own built-in (`dotnet.md` with `extends: dotnet`), which is the documented way to keep a built-in. A valid two-file setup therefore fails the build, and when only the child is listed the built-in parent is silently dropped from the output. Exempt `extends(local_parent) == parent` and emit the built-in before the local parent, or warn non-fatally when that parent is already resolved earlier in `out`. Add table rows for both orders.
findings.scenario:
config `presets: [dotnet, acme]`, local dotnet.md `---
extends: dotnet
---`, local acme.md `---
extends: dotnet
---` → prints base, built-in dotnet, local dotnet, acme (complete) but exits 1 with 'nested extends is not followed', so lean build stops. With `presets: [acme]` only: built-in dotnet is missing from the output.

findings.message: Scalar parsing exists twice and the copies disagree. `strip()` (config values) strips any mix of quote characters, while `extends()` uses a regex with a back-reference that requires matched quotes. The same malformed value is accepted in config.yaml and rejected in frontmatter, so config fails open (B6). Share one value parser that rejects mismatched quotes, and add config rows for `"node'` and `'node`.
findings.scenario: config.yaml `presets: ["node']` → read as `node`, exit 0. The frontmatter `extends: "node'` → error, exit 1 (the 'fm: mismatched quotes' row).

findings.message: Comment stripping only recognises a space before `#` (`split(" #")`), in both `strip()` and the frontmatter line at line 102. YAML also allows a tab before `#`, and a value with a tab-led comment is then rejected as malformed or unknown. Strip comments on `\s#` in the shared parser and add tab-comment rows for flow, block and frontmatter.
findings.scenario: config.yaml `presets: [node]\t# web` → 'malformed presets value', exit 1, build stops. `  - node\t# web` → "unknown preset 'node\t# web'". Frontmatter `extends: node\t# keep` → frontmatter error, exit 1.

findings.message: A second top-level `presets:` key is silently ignored; the first one wins. Warn when the key appears more than once.

`lookup(BUILTIN, …) or None` turns the 'refused' result (False) into None. A built-in that exists but is refused (for example a symlink out of the plugin presets dir) is then also reported as "unknown preset", which misstates the cause. The exit code is still 1. Keep False distinct from None.
`malformed presets value '{rest}'` interpolates raw config text into stderr. The other diagnostics use `!r`. Use `{rest!r}` so control characters cannot reach the terminal.

When `base` is also listed in `presets:`, it is resolved twice. The paths are deduped, but a local base.md frontmatter error or stray warning is printed twice. Dedupe the names before calling `resolve`.

Every line is `.strip()`ped before the frontmatter test, so an indented `   ---` on line 1 opens frontmatter and indented keys inside it are accepted. The README describes `---` as the first line. Strip only the line ending and BOM for the delimiter test.

The header's Exit list omits frontmatter errors (other key, unclosed, two extends), unreadable preset files and nested extends, although all of them exit 1. The README says only that they are 'reported'. Align both docs with the code.
